hints: Focus on what type of compound 3-methylpentan-2-one is, and what type of alcohol can form that functional group on oxidation.
Draw out 3-methylpentan-2-one as $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ and change the $\text{C=O}$ at carbon 2 back to $\text{CH-OH}$ to find the alcohol you need.
Look for the secondary alcohol with the OH on carbon 2 and the methyl branch on carbon 3, and check why tertiary alcohols cannot be oxidised this way.
walkthrough:
**Identify the target product**

First, let's be friends with the product. 3-methylpentan-2-one is a ketone.

The parent chain is pentan-2-one: $$\text{CH}_3-\text{C(=O)}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$$ with a methyl branch on carbon 3: $$\text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$$

**Recall alcohol oxidation rules**

Acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ is a strong oxidising agent, but the outcome depends on the alcohol class. Secondary alcohol to ketone (no change in carbon skeleton), primary alcohol to carboxylic acid, tertiary alcohol no reaction.

Rule to remember: $$\text{secondary alcohol } \text{R}_2\text{CHOH} \xrightarrow{[O]} \text{ketone } \text{R}_2\text{C=O}$$

**Work backwards to the precursor**

To make a ketone at carbon 2, we need the OH in exactly the same position before oxidation. So just replace C=O with CH-OH.

Required precursor is: $$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$$ This is 3-methylpentan-2-ol, a secondary alcohol.

**Match to the options**

Option D shows exactly this skeleton, with OH on carbon 2 and a methyl branch on carbon 3. Oxidation replaces the H on the $\text{CH-OH}$ with a double bond to O, giving the required ketone with no other change.

options.A: This is 2-methylpentan-2-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{C(OH)(CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. It is a tertiary alcohol with no H on the carbon bearing OH, so it resists oxidation by acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$. It cannot give a ketone.
options.B: This is 3-methylpentan-3-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C(OH)(CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. It is also a tertiary alcohol. Tertiary alcohols are not oxidised under these conditions, so this is a classic trap if you only count carbons but forget to check the alcohol class.
options.C: This molecule already contains the ketone group, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH(CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, plus a primary alcohol at the other end. Strong oxidation would oxidise the primary $-\text{OH}$ to a carboxylic acid, giving a keto-acid, not 3-methylpentan-2-one.
options.D: This is 3-methylpentan-2-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH(CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, a secondary alcohol. Oxidation removes the H from carbon 2 to form $\text{C=O}$ in the same position, giving $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH(CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, which is exactly 3-methylpentan-2-one.
